answer: The protocol requires each agent to store 1,000 unique data shards to ensure distinct utility. A verifier requests a random segment, which serves as a voyage into the storage depths; an honest agent incurs a baseline disk cost, whereas 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost by maintaining independent files. A sparrow alert audits every shard, and the agent must yield a sonnet of bits matching the proof-of-replication before the deadline.
